summary: /api/health now sits behind the standard API auth gate and answers 401 {"error":"Authentication required."} to unauthenticated callers — the exact contract the failed check named. The route no longer returns the generic API-404 for logged-in sessions either: it is a real, protected route returning a deterministic deployment fingerprint after login. Verified live on the dev preview and the production platform URL; the plain-502-on-domain observation was the separate edge routing issue. #10638 repro surface is now discoverable: every new QA run's chat advertises the /qase-test command, so the shutdown-threshold failure and the runtime-reuse block can be replayed from the interface alone.
what_was_done: Moved GET /api/health from before the /api auth gate to after it (commit 873f770): unauthenticated callers now get HTTP 401 {"error":"Authentication required."}; authenticated callers get the {status, service, accessMode, requestId} fingerprint
Every new QA run now starts with a system message advertising the /qase-test repro command, so the #10638 failure modes are discoverable through the QA interface (not just source code)
Updated the route contract in tests: 401 unauthenticated, 401 invalid token, 200 with fingerprint authenticated, unknown /api/* still 404 for authenticated callers
what_was_tested: Unauthenticated GET /api/health on the dev preview: 401 {"error":"Authentication required."}
Unauthenticated GET /api/health on the production platform URL: 401 {"error":"Authentication required."}
New run creation: session's first system message names /qase-test and both subcommands
Full automated test suite: 505 tests, 0 failures
